[1]

Complete PATH 001 CAREER PATHWAYS MOD 1, PATH 002 CAREER PATHWAYS MOD 2, and PATH 003 CAREER PATHWAYS MOD 3. [1]

Course titles and details: https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/AH-BA-HIST [1]

question: can you double major in political science and communication arts? how many credits total would i need to graduate
answer:
Yes. Political Science BA and Communication Arts BA are both listed as bachelor’s majors [16]. Ramapo allows a second major; students with two majors may double-count no more than half their courses and must complete all writing-intensive courses required for the second major [4][5].

You need at least 128 credits to graduate [6][7][9]; both majors’ recommended plans for students admitted in 2026–2027 also list 128 credits [1][2]. For residency, the Registrar FAQ says a minimum of 32 credits must be completed at Ramapo [6], while the graduation page requires at least 48 credits at Ramapo, including the final 32 in residence [7]. The pages differ on the Ramapo-credit minimum. The graduation page also says at least half the credits for each major/second major/minor must be completed at Ramapo [7].

Registrar: reg@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7695. Ask your adviser to review your course and credit plan [6].

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/AH-BA-COMM) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SO-BA-POLI) [4](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [5](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/faq/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/graduation-commencement/) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/policies/) [16](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs)

question: Does Intro to Philosophy count as a gen ed or only as a major elective for philosophy?
answer:
PHIL 101 Introduction to Philosophy is 4 credits and has no published prerequisites; it carries no General Education attribute [2, 14]. It is not among the named electives in the Philosophy BA requirements, so the catalog does not show it counting as a Philosophy major elective. [1]

The Philosophy BA (Bachelor of Arts) requires PHIL 106 Introduction to Logic and PHIL 201 World Wisdom Traditions; select 7 Philosophy electives from the listed options; select 1 upper-level course from the listed options; PHIL 400W Independent Study (Writing Intensive); and PATH 001, PATH 002, and PATH 003. The elective list includes an unnamed catalog entry, so I can’t confirm from the listed requirements whether PHIL 101 could qualify through that entry. [1] Philosophy Minor is also published. [1]

PHIL 101’s lack of a Gen Ed attribute distinguishes it from PHIL 106 (Quantitative Reasoning), PHIL 201 (Global Awareness), PHIL 143 (Historical Perspectives), and PHIL 205, 207, and 210 (Values and Ethics). [14]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/AH-BA-PHIL) [14](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs)

question: how many gen ed credits do i need total and do my major courses count toward any of them
answer:
Ramapo’s published requirements describe General Education as ten courses—not a fixed total number of credits: four keystone courses, one course in each of four keystone categories, and courses in two of three distribution categories [2]. The catalog says the curriculum should not exceed 41 credits [3].

Yes. No more than two General Education courses may double count toward both General Education and your major [3]. School Core courses may also count toward General Education or free electives for SSHS, HGS and CA; ASB School Core courses count toward ASB required courses [8]. Review your Degree Audit to see how courses apply: https://web.ramapo.edu/degree-audit-tools/ [8].

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/home/comprehensive-academic-plan/resources/)

question: what does the senior seminar in history cover and how many credits is it
answer:
The History BA lists HIST 410 CAPSTONE: HISTORICAL RESEARCH as a required course, but the provided catalog information does not give its description or credit value. [1]

The course titled LAWS 421 SENIOR SEMINAR is a different course, for Law and Society majors—not a history seminar. It is 4 credits. It focuses on developing a thesis topic and statement and completing the research needed for a Law and Society thesis. It is open only to Law and Society majors who are juniors or seniors intending to graduate in three semesters or less; students should contact the instructor for a permit to enroll. [2]

For details about HIST 410, contact the School of Arts, Humanities, and Education Office: AHEOffice@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7365, B-224.

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/AH-BA-HIST) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/LAWS421)

question: im a sophomore in psych, whats the recommended order of classes so i can graduate in 4 yrs? like what should i be taking junior year
answer:
The published Psychology BA plan is for students admitted to the major in 2024–2025, so check that it fits your admission year and completed courses. [1]

Junior year in that plan:
• Fall (16 credits): General Education Requirement; PSYC 303 – RESEARCH METHODS IN PSYCHOLOGY WI; PSYC 304 – DATA ANALYSIS IN PSYCHOLOGY; Psychology Elective. [1]
• Spring (16 credits): General Education Requirement; Category 5 Course: Clinical Perspectives; two Free Electives (minor, certificate, or second major requirement). [1]

The plan lists Category 6: Brain and Behavior and Category 7: (Fieldwork) WI for fourth-year fall, and Category 8 Capstone Seminar WI for fourth-year spring. It totals 128 credits and requires a 2.0 GPA. [1] Full plan: https://www.ramapo.edu/recommended-graduation-plan-2024/sshs/psychology/ [1]

Declare your major during sophomore year and before completing 64 credits. [5,8] At 64 credits, you’re considered a junior; if you haven’t completed Critical Reading and Writing and college-level math general education courses, a registration hold is placed until you register for them. [4]

Center for Student Success (Academic Advising): schedule a meeting with your faculty advisor for a junior graduation check-up, then review your degree evaluation to confirm you’re on track; the advisor lifts the hold after the meeting so you can register for Summer and Fall classes. [3] Email success@ramapo.edu or call (201) 684-7441; D-207. [3]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SO-BA-PSYC) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/advisement-by-year/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/advisement-by-year/)

question: should i add a minor in women and gender studies or just take more electives, which looks better for law school
answer:
There’s no verified information here on whether law schools prefer a minor or more electives, so I can’t say which looks better. Ramapo says an undergraduate degree includes free electives, and students may pursue a minor or second major [4]. A minor must include between 16 and 24 credits; major courses may overlap, but no more than half of the minor credits [6].

The catalog result for “women gender studies” lists: Women’s Gender & Sexuality Studies Minor; Africana Studies Minor; American Studies Minor; Contemplative Studies Minor; Crime and Justice Studies Minor; East Asian Studies Minor; English and Literary Studies Minor; Environmental Studies Minor [14].

If you decide to add a minor, the Registrar’s page says to review catalog requirements, email the convener to schedule a meeting, submit the online form, and not submit duplicate requests; after approval, the record updates within 5–7 days [8]. Another page says to pick up a declaration form at the Registrar or Center for Student Success, consult your advisor, get the convener’s signature, and return the form to the Registrar within a reasonable time before graduation [10]. The pages differ on the declaration steps. Registrar: reg@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7695, D-224 [8]. Center for Student Success (Academic Advising): success@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7441, D-207 [10].

Sources: [4](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [6](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/declare-major-minor-certificate/) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/faq/) [14](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs)
